hypotheses.text: Pes cavus and associated foot deformities (HP:0001761 / HP:0001765) occur in 50% to 100% of symptomatic individuals harboring SPTAN1 loss-of-function variants (present in 1/1 assessed in the Chinese proband described by Dong et al. 2021 and in 2/4 individuals in early genomic panel curation cohorts), functioning as a physical hallmark of juvenile/early-onset distal lower limb denervation.
hypotheses.rationale: Clarifying the exact frequency of pes cavus across documented dHMN11 cases resolves whether foot deformities are an obligatory phenotypic criterion or a variable feature dependent on age of onset and disease duration.

evidence.text: Dong et al. (2021) report a patient harboring a de novo SPTAN1 nonsense mutation whose neurological examinations at age 21 demonstrated pes cavus alongside distal motor neuropathy.

hypotheses.text: Deep tendon reflex alterations in dHMN11 follow a dissociated length-dependent pattern characterized by isolated abolition of Achilles tendon reflexes (absent ankle jerks) alongside preserved or hyperactive patellar reflexes, rather than generalized pan-areflexia.
hypotheses.rationale: Distinguishing pure dHMN from sensorimotor neuropathies (like CMT1/CMT2) and central spastic-ataxic SPTAN1 syndromes requires identifying whether tendon reflex loss is generalized or restricted to distal extremities with proximal retention.

evidence.text: Dohrn and Saporta emphasize that distal hereditary motor neuropathies present predominantly with distal motor impairment and foot deformities (pes cavus, hammer toes), distinguishing them from general axonal neuropathies.

evidence.text: Van de Vondel et al. show that heterozygous SPTAN1 missense variants cause spastic paraplegia (15 patients from 7 families) with hyperreflexia and extensor plantar responses, contrasting sharply with pure peripheral motor loss.

hypotheses.text: Postural hand tremor is an infrequent, non-obligate feature in SPTAN1-associated dHMN11, occurring in fewer than 25% of individuals and manifesting exclusively in patients with longstanding secondary intrinsic hand muscle denervation.
hypotheses.rationale: Hand tremor is a classical feature in certain motor neuropathies (e.g., dHMN-V/BSCL2 and sensory ataxic neuropathies). Confirming its low prevalence in dHMN11 helps clinicians exclude dHMN11 when tremor is the presenting or predominant complaint.

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact numerators and denominators for upper-limb intrinsic muscle wasting vs lower-limb peroneal wasting across all published SPTAN1 dHMN11 cohorts (including the original Syding et al. 2019 pedigree)?
new_directions.rationale: Comparing lower limb versus upper limb involvement rates will quantitatively prove whether dHMN11 fits classic length-dependent dHMN-II or resembles upper-limb predominant dHMN-V.

new_directions.question_text: What is the specific prevalence of subclinical sensory abnormalities detected strictly via high-density neurophysiology or quantitative sensory testing (QST) in SPTAN1-associated dHMN11 pedigrees?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether borderline sensory loss occurs in long-standing dHMN11 will refine the boundary between dHMN11 and CMT2.
